origin: GTA amalgamation history, popularized by Drake
definition: Toronto's most famous nickname. Refers to the 1998 amalgamation of six municipalities — old Toronto, North York, Etobicoke, Scarborough, York and East York — into one city, and doubles as a nod to the 416 area code. Toronto rapper Jimmy Prime used it in street culture first; Drake globalized it with his 2015 album 'Views From The 6.'
example: "You coming back to the 6 for the summer?"

definition: An old-school nickname for Toronto — a play on "T.O.," itself short for Toronto, Ontario. Still used by people who think "the 6ix" is played out.
example: "Born and raised in T Dot, never leaving."

definition: Even shorter version of T Dot. Just "the Dot."
example: "He's not from the Dot, he's a 905 kid."

definition: How "Toronto" actually sounds when locals say it fast — the middle "o" and "t" basically disappear.
example: "I'm from Tranna, not TOR-ON-TO."

definition: A 19th-century nickname for Toronto. Originally an insult from smaller Ontario towns annoyed that Toronto politicians "hogged" the provincial legislature — later reinforced by the city's massive William Davies meatpacking plant. Toronto eventually owned the name instead of fighting it.
example: "Real ones still call it Hogtown."

definition: Toronto's original telephone area code, used as shorthand for the old City of Toronto / downtown core — sometimes with an implied "real Toronto" vs. the suburbs.
example: "He reps 416 hard, won't even come north of Eglinton."

definition: The area code covering the suburban ring around Toronto — Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, Markham, Pickering and more. Used to describe someone from "outside the city," sometimes as light shade.
example: "Nah he's 905, he needs GPS to find the subway."

definition: Greater Toronto Area — Toronto plus the surrounding regions (Peel, York, Durham, Halton). Used constantly in everyday speech, not just on government maps.
example: "Biggest show in the GTA this weekend."

definition: Short for Scarborough, the large district in Toronto's east end known for its own distinct slang and hip-hop scene.
example: "He's out in Scarbs, near Kennedy."

origin: Neighbourhood, cultural touchstone for GTA slang
definition: The intersection and surrounding neighbourhood in northwest Toronto, shaped heavily by Jamaican, Somali and other Caribbean/African communities. Along with Scarborough and Rexdale, it's one of the corridors most credited with shaping modern Toronto slang.
example: "That word's been around since Jane and Finch, way before it went viral."

origin: Highway 401, busiest highway in North America
definition: Highway 401, the mega-highway cutting through Toronto — famously the busiest stretch of highway in North America. "Taking the 401" is a whole personality trait.
example: "401's a parking lot right now, take Eglinton instead."

definition: The Gardiner Expressway, the elevated highway running along Lake Ontario through downtown. Just "the Gardiner" — nobody says the full name.
example: "Take the Gardiner, it'll be faster than downtown streets."

definition: The Don Valley Parkway, connecting downtown to the 401. Locals affectionately call it the "Don Valley Parking Lot" because it's almost always jammed.
example: "Avoid the DVP after 4, it's a parking lot."

definition: Steeles Avenue, the street that marks Toronto's northern city limit. "North of Steeles" means you've left the city for York Region.
example: "That's north of Steeles, that's not even Toronto."

origin: UK/Caribbean street slang, common across the GTA
definition: Your neighbourhood, home turf, or the area you grew up in.
example: "Come through the endz this weekend, everyone's around."

origin: TTC branding since the 1954 red subway cars
definition: Nickname for the TTC (Toronto's transit system), dating back to the red-painted subway cars that debuted in 1954. The TTC still uses "Ride the Rocket" in its own marketing.
example: "I'm just gonna ride the Rocket down, parking's brutal."

definition: The older, more literal version of "the Rocket" — a direct reference to the red subway trains and streetcars.
example: "Caught the red rocket just in time."

definition: The overnight TTC bus routes (like Blue Night buses) that run after the subway closes and the bars let out — named for, well, exactly what you'd expect happens on them.
example: "Missed the last subway, guess it's the vomit comet home."

origin: Jamaican Patois, via Toronto's Caribbean community
definition: Used as a stand-in for "I" or "me" — a self-referential term believed to come from Jamaican Patois as spoken in Toronto's Caribbean communities. The whole "Toronto mans" identity is built around this word.
example: "It was freezing out, mans had to grab a jacket."

definition: Originally Jamaican Patois for "those men" or "my people." In Toronto it's used loosely for your crew or group of friends, regardless of who's actually in it.
example: "Pulled up with the man dem to the game."

origin: Jamaican Patois for close friend / brother
definition: A close friend or brother — a term of real loyalty and trust, above casual friendship.
example: "That's my bredren, known him since grade school."

definition: Brother, friend, day-one. Popularized by Toronto rap and now used well outside music circles.
example: "Good looks, brodie, appreciate you."

origin: General diaspora/street slang, common in Toronto
definition: Close friend or crew — used the way "family" is used, but for people you're actually close with day to day.
example: "What's good, fam?"

definition: Someone lazy, unmotivated or generally useless — a "waste yute" is the younger version of the same insult.
example: "He never shows up on time, such a wasteman."

definition: Short for "opposition" — enemies, rivals, people you're beefing with.
example: "Don't go over there, that's opp territory."

definition: The block or area belonging to your opps — enemy territory.
example: "You already know not to be posted on the opp block."

definition: To show respect, give credit, or hype someone up. Literally "to big yourself/someone up."
example: "Big up to everyone who came out tonight."

definition: A greeting or farewell rooted in reggae culture, expressing unity and goodwill.
example: "Alright, I'm out — one love."

definition: "Thank you" or "I appreciate that," delivered with real sincerity. "Nuff" here means "enough," as in "plenty."
example: "You helped me move that whole apartment — nuff respect."

definition: Used as an acknowledgment or a casual goodbye — similar to saying "cool" or "take care."
example: "Appreciate it, safe."

definition: "What's going on?" / "What's up?" — one of the most common Patois-rooted greetings heard across the GTA.
example: "Wagwan, haven't seen you in mad long."

definition: A tag question meaning "right?" or "isn't that so?" — tacked onto the end of a statement to get agreement.
example: "That game was cold, ahlie?"

definition: An emphatic filler used at the end of a sentence for emphasis, similar to "though" or "for real."
example: "I'm not even mad, styll."

origin: Street/hip-hop slang, common in the GTA
definition: "For real" — used to confirm something is genuinely true.
example: "He pulled up at 6am to help, for tru."

origin: Arabic, common via Toronto's Somali and Arab communities
definition: "I swear to God" in Arabic — used constantly across the GTA thanks to the city's large Somali and Arab communities, well beyond just those speaking Arabic at home.
example: "Wallahi I'm not lying, ask anyone who was there."

origin: Widely used across North American street slang, common in Toronto
definition: Seriously, no joke — used to stress that you mean exactly what you said.
example: "Deadass, that was the best patty I've ever had."

definition: Trash talk — an insult or dig thrown at someone, especially rooted in Canadian hockey culture where players "chirp" opponents. In everyday Toronto speech it just means friendly (or not-so-friendly) roasting.
example: "Stop chirping me, it's not that deep."

origin: Jamaican Patois, crossed over via Caribbean community
definition: Extremely attractive or impressive.
example: "Bro that new whip is leng."

origin: UK/Caribbean street slang, widely used in the GTA
definition: Excellent, attractive or high-quality — can describe food, people, outfits or music.
example: "This jerk chicken is peng."

definition: Means the opposite of its dictionary definition — "a lot" or "very," not "empty."
example: "There's bare people at the mall today."

origin: General North American street slang, everyday in Toronto
definition: An intensifier meaning "very" or "a lot," unrelated to anger.
example: "That line was mad long."

origin: UK-influenced street slang, common in the GTA
definition: Something unfortunate, unfair or genuinely bad. "That's peak" means "that sucks."
example: "Missed the last train by two minutes — that's peak."

definition: High, particularly from smoking marijuana.
example: "He's been blem since the concert started."

origin: Caribbean/UK street slang, everyday GTA usage
definition: To meet up or hang out with someone — in a romantic context, it can mean seeing or dating someone casually.
example: "Let's link up after work."

origin: African American Vernacular English, used in GTA rap slang
definition: Money.
example: "He's out here making gwap."

origin: Hip-hop/drill slang, widely used in the GTA scene
definition: Money, usually in reference to a substantial amount ($1,000 or a stack of bills).
example: "Spent racks on that jacket."

origin: Hip-hop slang, common across the GTA
definition: Money, or a financial opportunity. "Secure the bag" means locking down something profitable.
example: "Two jobs this summer — just trying to secure the bag."

origin: Hip-hop slang, widely used in the GTA scene
definition: Large amounts of money, typically counted in thousands (a "band" = $1,000, named after the paper band around a stack of bills).
example: "Saved up bands from working all summer."

definition: The Toronto Raptors' rallying slogan, unveiled in April 2014 ahead of the playoffs. It grew into a citywide identity — Canada's only NBA team representing the whole country, not just the city.
example: "We The North, no explanation needed."

definition: "October's Very Own" — Drake's Toronto-based record label and clothing brand, named for his October birthday. Shorthand for the whole OVO/Drake cultural footprint on the city.
example: "He's got the OVO owl on his jacket."

definition: A neighbourhood in Etobicoke, in Toronto's northwest — alongside Scarborough and Jane-Finch, one of the inner-suburb communities most credited with shaping Toronto's street vocabulary and hip-hop scene.
example: "He's from Rexdale, grew up around Dixon."

definition: A neighbourhood in Scarborough with a strong cultural identity in Toronto rap and street life — often name-checked the way other cities name-check specific blocks.
example: "That's a Malvern thing, you wouldn't get it."

origin: UK street slang, widely adopted across the GTA
definition: Someone street-smart, always out and about, who knows how things really work on the ground — not a compliment or an insult on its own, just a description.
example: "He's a real roadman, knows everyone downtown."

definition: Young people, or your friends/crew — a Patois-rooted pronunciation of "youths" that stuck as its own word.
example: "Me and the youts are pulling up later."

origin: General affirmation, common across the GTA
definition: A catch-all positive response — used as a greeting, a farewell, or a reaction to good news. When plans are locked in, they're "blessed."
example: "See you Friday then — blessed."

origin: GTA street slang, stylized spelling of "starved"
definition: Extremely hungry — the drawn-out spelling is part of the word.
example: "I'm maaarved, let's reach Markham station and grab something."

origin: Hip-hop/streetwear slang, widely used in the GTA
definition: A person's style, fashion sense and overall presentation — having "drip" means dressing with consistent, impressive style.
example: "New chain, new kicks — the drip is unmatched today."

origin: Short for "outfit," widely used in the GTA
definition: Short for "outfit" — everything you're wearing, as a whole look.
example: "Where'd you get that fit from, it's clean."

origin: General hip-hop slang, everyday GTA usage
definition: Sharp, stylish, well put-together — used for outfits, cars, sneakers, basically anything that looks good.
example: "That whip is clean."

definition: Literally "thing" in Patois, but used constantly for a romantic interest ("my ting") or just to refer to an unspecified person, object or situation.
example: "Is that your new ting I saw you with?"

definition: Lame, disappointing, not up to standard — a step below "peak" but the same general idea.
example: "They ran out of patties already? That's weak."

definition: Blunt, unenthusiastic or straight-up boring — describing a person's response or a whole situation with no energy to it.
example: "He gave a dry reply, didn't even ask how I was."

definition: Being wishy-washy, flaky or sus (suspicious) — someone who can't be trusted to be straight with you.
example: "Don't trust him, he's mad mix up."

origin: General hip-hop slang, everyday GTA usage
definition: As a verb, to show off or stunt. Tacked onto a noun, it can also mean you're about to go do something ("gym flex" = heading to the gym).
example: "He's flexing that new watch on every story."

definition: A drawn-out exclamation for when something needs a reaction — shock, disbelief, or someone getting on your nerves.
example: "Hooooly, did you see that?"

definition: Short for "allow it" — let it go, don't worry about it, drop the subject.
example: "'Llow it, it's not even that deep."

origin: AAVE, widely used across the GTA
definition: "No lie" — "cap" means a lie, so "no cap" means you're telling the truth.
example: "That was the best show I've been to, no cap."

definition: The Jamaican beef (or chicken, or veggie) patty — a flaky, curry-coloured pastry sold at corner stores and bakeries across the city. Not slang exactly, but non-negotiable Toronto cultural vocabulary.
example: "Grab me a patty and a coco bread on your way."

definition: A Caribbean flatbread wrapped around curried meat, chickpeas or vegetables — a GTA staple order, especially in Scarborough.
example: "Say less, we're getting roti after this."
